#2283. Luc Chabert rêvait d'affronter les Verts

Coprésident du GFA Rumilly Vallières (N1), le réputé fromager Luc Chabert explique au Dauphiné Libéré pourquoi il est si content d'affronter les Verts demain après-midi à Annecy. Extraits.

"Mon père Gérard partait à Geoffroy-Guichard les soirs de Coupe d’Europe. Il était même présent à Glasgow en 1976, il est rentré 4 jours après ! On a toujours vécu avec le maillot vert à la maison. Mon père était président de l’ES Vallières, on jouait en vert. L’origine de la couleur du maillot, c’est l’ASSE. Donc, petit, j’ai baigné dans le vert entre l’ASSE et Vallières. Je crois que c’était la première fois que nous tombions dans le même chapeau que Saint-Étienne. Quand j’ai vu le groupe, j’ai envoyé un SMS à mon fils, Edgar, lui aussi supporter des Verts. Depuis le temps qu’on rêvait de jouer l’ASSE en Coupe de France, notre rêve s’est réalisé !

On a eu des super relations avec les dirigeants stéphanois pour l’organisation du match. Les planètes se sont alignées. Sans le FC Annecy, nous n’aurions pas pu organiser un tel rendez-vous. Et sans la complicité de l’ASSE, on n’aurait pas pu jouer le dimanche après-midi. Ils seront très bien accueillis. Le match, on va le jouer pour le gagner, c’est une certitude. Surtout, on va le vivre pleinement car on n’a aucune pression. On accueillera quoi qu’il arrive le résultat avec fierté et la satisfaction du travail bien fait. Et si l’aventure continue, on sera les plus heureux."

#2281. Onorato: "Flaminio-Lazio? Capienza sui 46-48.000 posti…"

Questa mattina sulle frequenze di Radiosei è intervenuto l'Assessore Alessandro Onorato per commentare la situazione relativa alla Lazio e lo Stadio Flaminio

Questa mattina sulle frequenze di Radiosei è intervenuto l'Assessore Alessandro Onorato per commentare la situazione relativa alla Lazio e lo Stadio Flaminio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La Roma sullo stadio è avanti perchè ha iniziato oltre due anni prima. La vicenda Flaminio è complessa, così come il rapporto di Lotito con i tifosi. Vorrei chiarire un dato, noi rappresentiamo l’amministrazione pubblica, conta solo l’interesse pubblico di recuperare questo stadio che è in una situazione vergognosa. Il primo dato certo è che il progetto della Lazio è reale e solido e c’è stata una prima chiusura importante della conferenza dei servizi. Di fatto c’è stato un primo assenso tecnico da parte di istituzioni che riguardano comune, regione e stato. Sostanzialmente c’è una positività, ma con delle prescrizioni. La Soprintendenza ha posto una raccomandazione sull’altezza, per dirne una.

Oggi le cose stanno che dopo la chiusura della conferenza dei servizi, la Lazio deve integrare una serie di pareri, a partire proprio dalla Soprintendenza dello Stato, sulla capienza. Una cosa sono 50mila posti, un’altra 47mila. Questo è il tema in discussione, alla fine potrebbe essere tra 46mila e 48mila. Siamo al punto che la Lazio ha integrato il suo piano, ci sarà una risposta da parte della Soprintendenza. Superate queste risposte, la palla passerà al Comune. Confidiamo che questo iter si possa concludere anche entro Natale. Ovviamente, se e quando ci arriveranno questi documenti per poter dare o meno l’interesse pubblico. Il Comune di Roma ha tutto l’interesse a dare una risposta. E’ finita l’era del non si può fare. Ottenuto l’interesse pubblico saremmo al 50% dell’opera. A quel punto sarebbe nelle mani della Lazio. Ottenuto l’ok delle istituzioni pubbliche, mi sembrerebbe inverosimile che una società possa tornare indietro.

Mi sento di dire che lo stadio Flaminio possa essere una grande operazione per il club e per la città. Se un privato mette questi soldi mi sembra una cosa buona e giusta. Fare anche un investimento di 500 milioni, per una società sportiva quotata in borsa può essere una buona opportunità. Aspetterei a dire che i soldi non ci sono, non credo che un soggetto giuridico ed economico sia pazzo nell’investire dei soldi già nella fase di progettazione. Le procedure sono folli e lunghe, noi abbiamo velocizzato nel rispetto delle norme. Non si può perdere tempo.

Non parlerei di nemici, ma di un dato di fatto. E’ evidente che chi abita intorno al Flaminio non vuole che lo stadio venga rifatto. Ma questa è una realtà che noi dobbiamo affrontare. Capisco la preoccupazione degli abitanti, ma anche qui dobbiamo decidere. Tutti vogliano andare allo stadio e nessuno vuole un fastidio in quel momento specifico.

#2280. Le Vert interdit à Annecy

Une nouvelle fois, le déplacement des supporters stéphanois à Annecy pour le match du 7ème tour de la Coupe de France contre le GFA Rumilly Vallières, demain à 15 heures, sera fortement encadré.

En effet, la Préfecture de Haute-Savoie a défini un arrêté d’encadrement et de périmètre. Outre l'encadrement habituel des supporters se rendant dans le parcage, l'arrêté vise toute personne se prévalant supporter de l'ASSE qui aura l'interdiction de se rendre dans le centre-ville d'Annecy ou au bord du lac. Pour ces supporters en véhicule léger, un parking est disponible (places limitées, environ 300 places). Pour accéder à ce parking, il faudra être muni d'un macaron d’accès.Parmi les raisons invoquées à ces encadremets et interdictions, figure la crainte de voir débarquer à Annecy des ultras grenoblois et lyonnais.

#2277. Lucas Stassin passeur et presque buteur

Les Diablotins belges de Lucas Stassin ont obtenu hier, à Essen, un succès de prestige en s'imposant 1-2 face à leurs homologues allemands.

Lucas Stassin a été passeur décisif à deux reprises.Tout d'abord, après un débordement côté droit, il a offert, à la 8ème, d'un centre en retrait, la balle de but au vilain Julian Duranville.Juste avant la pause, il a eu l'occasion de faire le break, mais son tir a trouvé le poteau du gardien allemand.Ensuite, à la réception, au 1er poteau d'un centre venu de la gauche, il a effectué une talonnade,  qui a permis à Roméo Vermant d'inscrire le but de la victoire à la 65ème minute. Qualifiés pour l'Euro espoirs 2027, les Diablotins disputeront un deuxième match amical contre l'Italie, lundi à 18h15 à Livourne.

1er but : 30"     Tir sur le poteau : 2'50"       2ème but : 4'

#2275. Sebastian Grønning explains how Hertha have turned things around in Berlin

After several turbulent years, Hertha finally appear to be moving in the right direction. Following relegation from the Bundesliga in 2023 and successive campaigns in which promotion proved elusive, the capital club have made an excellent start to the new 2. Bundesliga season.

Hertha sit top of the table after 11 matches, having won 10 of their opening 11 fixtures, and the feeling around the Olympiastadion is increasingly one of optimism.

Speaking in an interview with Bundesliga media, Grønning admitted that such a flying start was not necessarily expected following a summer of significant squad changes. However, the early performances quickly gave the players belief that something special was developing.

“From the friendly matches and then from the first two competitive games of the season, we got the feeling that, hey, we really have something here that we can build on,” Grønning explained.

“That confidence boost from game to game and from win to win has naturally given us that boost and that confidence in believing that we’re doing something right here.”

For the striker, one of the biggest differences compared to previous campaigns has been the clarity within the squad, with every player understanding their individual responsibilities.

“I would say our philosophy is quite clear for every player in the team. We know what role each one of us has, what we have to bring and what we have to do,” he continued.

“When we put all these roles together, I think we have a very good harmony and very good chemistry in the team.”

Grønning also highlighted Hertha’s physical intensity, believing their ability to maintain an attacking approach even when protecting leads has helped distinguish them from their promotion rivals.

A significant part of Hertha’s transformation has been the influence of head coach Stefan Leitl, who has now had the opportunity to shape the squad more closely around his footballing philosophy.

Grønning was particularly complimentary of the 49-year-old, praising his tactical understanding, communication and ability to recognise the strengths of his players.

“He’s really good at recognising what kinds of players he has and to build the team around these players. Then he’s a very clear communicator,” the striker said.

After arriving in Berlin towards the end of the 2024/25 season and having overseen several key departures amid financial uncertainty, Leitl has now used this summer to put his stamp on the squad. Grønning believes the current group is much more representative of the coach’s ideas following significant recruitment activity.

“I think this year he had a bigger impact in terms of recruiting players, in terms of the style and to fit these together. So I think it’s fair to say that this is more his team.”

The Danish forward also made it clear that he has personally embraced Leitl’s approach, suggesting the coach has earned the trust of the dressing room.

“I’m really buying into how we want to do things this year. And I’m really buying into his ideas. I want to play for him really very much.”

Despite the remarkable start, Grønning recognises that the relationship between Hertha and their supporters has been shaped by several years of disappointment.

The club’s relegation in 2023 has been followed by three frustrating seasons in the 2. Bundesliga, with hopes of a return to the top flight failing to materialise each time.

Consequently, while improved performances have brought renewed excitement to the Olympiastadion, the striker believes everyone must remain patient rather than getting carried away with promotion expectations.

“I also think the fans heard it from the past and have these scars of believing in the best outcome, and Hertha can get them hurt or disappointed, you know?” he admitted.

Grønning believes the only way to change that narrative is through continued performances on the pitch.

“Both the fans and us as a team have to just stay calm and keep following this path of focusing on each game and putting that energy and effort into it.”

Nevertheless, the opportunity to be part of a Hertha side that finally secures promotion is clearly something that motivates him.

“Every player feels the same as me that it would be great if I could be a part of that team that brings Hertha back where they belong,” Grønning explained.

“They deserve to be in the Bundesliga and fans deserve to see Bundesliga football.”

However, he was quick to acknowledge that there is still a long way to go, with plenty of challenges remaining before promotion becomes a reality.

On a personal level, the Danish striker is also determined to keep developing his game, having established himself as a traditional centre-forward whose greatest strengths lie in his positioning, movement and finishing inside the penalty area.

“I’m a classic box striker. I need to have service in the box. I’m very strong in and around the box with my finishing, with my positioning, with my timing,” he explained.

Grønning also revealed that he regularly stays behind after training to work on his finishing, highlighting the attention to detail within Hertha’s coaching setup.

Even after finding the net, however, he insists there is no room for complacency.

“It’s not that after a goal everything is good and everything is positive. So it’s just about the process and you have to trust that,” he added.

For Hertha, that mentality perhaps reflects the wider approach currently being adopted in Berlin. There is renewed confidence, a clear identity and a squad that appears increasingly comfortable with its responsibilities.

The memories of previous disappointments have not disappeared, but with Hertha leading the 2. Bundesliga after 11 matches, the foundations for a genuine promotion challenge are beginning to look increasingly convincing.

#2271. Careless Liverpool concede same goal twice in second-half capitulation against Leeds

Leeds United came from 2-0 down at half-time to beat Liverpool 4-2 at Soldier Field in Chicago as Andoni Iraola’s side were undone by sloppy defending in the second period.

Liverpool’s dominant first-half display was underlined by goals from Luke Chambers and Florian Wirtz. However, Daniel Farke’s men replied with four strikes in 25 second-half minutes through Sean Longstaff, Brenden Aaronson and two alarmingly similar goals from Dominic Calvert-Lewin.

🎯 "CALVERT-LEWIN ARRIVES!" pic.twitter.com/CaHOeXQn7E

🤩 "Calvert-Lewin makes it FOUR!" pic.twitter.com/mEEi882OWi

Liverpool centre-back Chambers, 22, who spent last season on loan at Charlton Athletic, opened the scoring on seven minutes, pouncing on a Dominik Szoboszlai corner which had been flicked on at the near post by Milos Kerkez.

Jeremie Frimpong, serviced by a wonderfully flighted cross-field ball by Trey Nyoni, then set up Wirtz to make it 2-0 five minutes before the break, but on the hour Leeds began their recovery when Aaronson scored following a mistake by Kerkez – who gave up possession to Ethan Ampadu in his own half.

GOAL! Aaronson pulls one back! 2-1 pic.twitter.com/tdy17cITSd

Ampadu’s long throw was flicked on to Calvert-Lewin to level the score, then minutes later Curtis Jones’s carelessness allowed Longstaff in to put Leeds in front.

🔥 "LONGSTAFF! WHAT A TURNAROUND!" pic.twitter.com/G9LvLIk0Mi

And it was a familiar story five minutes from time when Ampadu’s throw again prompted chaos in Liverpool’s back line, allowing Calvert-Lewin to steal in front of Jones and seal victory.

Liverpool return to Anfield for friendlies against Monaco and Como before they begin their Premier League season away at Newcastle United later this month.

Leeds have matches against RB Leipzig, Manchester United and Augsburg before their league campaign gets under way at Nottingham Forest.

July 25- Leeds 2 Wrexham 3July 30- Leeds 1 Sunderland 0Today- Leeds 4 Liverpool 2August 8- Leeds vs RB LeipzigAugust 12- Leeds vs Manchester UnitedAugust 15- Leeds vs Augsburg

July 25- Liverpool 4 Sunderland 2July 30- Liverpool 1 Wrexham 0Today- Liverpool 2 Leeds 4August 9- Liverpool vs MonacoAugust 16- Liverpool vs Como x2

Possession: Liverpool 57%-43% LeedsShots: 9-15Shots on target: 3-7Corners: 3-7

The final whistle is blown in Chicago and that has well and truly been a game of two halves. At half-time, Liverpool were in complete control with a 2-0 lead. However, four Leeds goals in 25 second-half minutes have given Daniel Farke’s side the victory at Soldier Field. Both sides will now return home to the UK.

Aaronson is booked for a cynical pull on Ramsay.

Koumas should score for Liverpool. He is played in behind and for some strange reason Cairns comes a long way out of his goal. Koumas should lift it over Cairns and into the empty net but gets his chip wrong and the shot goes off target.

Leeds’ second half gets even better and Liverpool’s gets even worse. It is a very similar goal to Calvert-Lewin’s first; Ampadu’s long throw is flicked on and Calvert-Lewin meets it, heading past Mamardashvili. This is very much your game of two halves.

Daniel Farke is making a double change as Gnonto and Lienou come on.

Frimpong kicks the ball out of play and he may have a problem. Is it just cramp or more serious than that? He is going to come off and be replaced by Scanlon.

Leeds have come from 2-0 down to lead 3-2 in Chicago. Aaronson’s cross from the left side of the box should be cleared by Jones but he does not put his foot through it. Instead, that allows Longstaff to slot home past Mamardashvili. Leeds have scored three goals in a quarter of an hour.

Leeds are on level terms. A long throw from Ampadu out on the left is flicked on at the near post and Calvert-Lewin has the easiest of tap-ins at the back post. Liverpool were in cruise control at 2-0 up at the break but not have not been at it since half-time.

Justin is played in behind down the left channel and tries to pick out Calvert-Lewin in the centre of the box but Ndiaye steps in with a crucial interception.

Andoni Iraola is going to make a quadruple change. Elliott, Ramsay, Ndiaye and Tsimikas all come on. Szoboszlai is one of those to head off and hands Jones the armband.

Liverpool were much the better side in the first half but have not really been at the races since the break.

Leeds punish Kerkez’s error and get a goal back. Kerkez gifts the ball away inside his own half and Ampadu picks up not far outside the Liverpool penalty area. He spots the run of Aaronson to his left and slides it into the American, who takes one touch before sliding it underneath Mamardashvili and into the Liverpool net.

Wilson is fouled down Leeds’ right and he will take the free-kick. The Welshman clips it in and picks out Calvert-Lewin, whose header goes well wide of the target.

Calvert-Lewin gets a touch past Ndukwe just inside the Liverpool half and drives towards the Liverpool penalty area. It is difficult to know whether it is a shot or a cross from Calvert-Lewin and the ball goes wide of the far post. Bogle did make a run towards the back post and was hoping Calvert-Lewin would pick him out.

Liverpool negotiate a couple of long throws and a corner from Leeds in quick succession.

After Ndukwe’s pass inside his own half is intercepted, Justin decides to shoot from range but Mamardashvili easily saves.

Liverpool have made a number of changes at the break, with Chiesa, Jones, Gravenberch and Koumas all coming on. It takes an absolute age for Leeds to re-emerge, with Liverpool coming back out from the tunnel nearly ten minutes before Leeds. What on earth is going on in the Leeds dressing room at the break? This is ridiculous from Leeds.

The second half begins more than 20 minutes after the first ended. To be exact, 23 minutes is the gap. Calvert-Lewin is one of a few changes at half-time for Leeds, as is former Liverpool man Wilson. We are back under way in Chicago.

Jeremie 🔗 Flo 😍 pic.twitter.com/kxwhYA845Q

Andoni Iraola said before the game that Florian Wirtz would play 45 minutes in his first game of pre-season so we can expect him and Alexander Isak to come off at half-time.

Stateside Reds enjoying the action 🤩 pic.twitter.com/hfwaLmi8xB

Possession: Liverpool 60%-40% LeedsShots: 5-6Shots on target: 3-2Corners: 1-3

The first half is brought to an end and Liverpool take a 2-0 lead into the break courtesy of goals from Chambers and Wirtz.

Szoboszlai clips a delightful cross from the right all the way to the back post, aiming to pick out the run of Kerkez. A goal-kick is given, with the referee deciding the last touch came off Kerkez, but the Hungarian left-back is not happy with that decision. The replays prove why as the last touch came off Bogle.

There will be four minutes of added time at the end of this first half due to the Gudmundsson injury in particular.

Leeds have been forced into one change in this half and they might be forced into another here. As Wirtz scored, two Leeds players collided, which has resulted in Ampadu staying down and receiving treatment. The Leeds captain though does seem to be ok after receiving some treatment.

It is a lovely team goal from Liverpool to take them 2-0 up around five minutes before half-time. Nyoni’s flat ball out to the right side of the box is volleyed first time back across the box by Frimpong. Wirtz runs onto the ball and, from the penalty spot, slots the ball home past Cairns.

After Nyoni makes an interception inside his own half, Liverpool counter. The ball is shifted out to the left, where Ngumoha drives at Bogle. Ngumoha’s step-over takes him past Bogle inside the Leeds penalty area and he drives the ball across the six-yard box but no-one in a Liverpool shirt is on hand to tap it in. Should Isak have done a better job to get on the end of that one? Possibly.

Szoboszlai, who loves scoring free-kick stunners, blasts the free-kick into the wall.

Gudmundsson’s day is indeed over and is replaced by Bornauw, which could see a shift for Leeds.

Ngumoha is brought down by Bogle inches outside the Leeds penalty area out on the left. It was very, very close to being a penalty but was just outside the box. Before the free-kick will be taken, Leeds look like they will be forced into a change as Gudmundsson has gone down clutching at his right hamstring.

For the second time in a few minutes, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception. Wirtz slides a pass through into the Leeds box on the left to pick out the run of Ngumoha. Just as Ngumoha was getting his shot away from around eight yards out, Rodon slides in to intercept. However, the offside flag goes up against Ngumoha anyway.

Wirtz and Isak link up really well inside the Leeds half, with the latter putting a touch beyond one Leeds defender and runs towards the Leeds penalty area. However, Rodon steps in with a crucial interception to take it off Isak.

Nmecha scored from long range for Leeds the other day against Sunderland and he is not far off adding another long-range goal to his pre-season tally. His effort from just outside the box is dragged just wide of Mamardashvili’s right post.

Frimpong drives forward from inside his own half and takes Liverpool through the Leeds half before he is cynically pulled down by Tanaka, who is rightly booked. Sometimes in a pre-season friendly players might get away with that but this referee does not show mercy to Tanaka.

That is nearly a horror moment for Cairns in the Leeds goal. He rolls the ball out from his own box and Isak just about gets a touch on it but fortunately for Leeds it does not end in a horror show for Cairns.

Frimpong lays it across to Nyoni in a central position outside the box and the latter takes on the shot. Nyoni goes for accuracy over power and looks for the bottom corner but Cairns gets down to his left to make the save.

Chance for Leeds. Bogle whips in a cross from the right touchline and picks out the head of Nmecha, whose effort is saved well by Mamardashvili down to his right.

Liverpool hit the front in Chicago. Szoboszlai’s outswinger corner from the right is flicked on at the front post by Kerkez and is met by Chambers, who smashes home on the half volley into the Leeds net.

Liverpool counter from their own box after defending a long throw through Isak and Frimpong, whose cross from the right is deflected behind for the first corner of the game...

The pitch is not looking in the best condition, which perhaps is not a massive surprise when you consider that Chicago Fire played here last night. They beat Charlotte 2-1, with Robert Lewandowski scoring twice.

Gudmundsson is back to his feet after some treatment but is breathing quite heavily. It does appear that the Swedish wing-back should be fine to continue.

After Liverpool clear a Leeds long throw into the Liverpool penalty area, Gudmundsson goes down clutching at his lower back after an awkward landing and play is halted.

We are under way at Soldier Field. It is not too hot in Chicago today, with the temperature a touch over 20 degrees at kick-off.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel and we are just moments away from kick-off at Soldier Field in Chicago. You’ll Never Walk Alone rings around the stadium as the teams emerge.

Liverpool: Mamardashvili; Frimpong, Ndukwe, Chambers, Kerkez; Nyoni, Szoboszlai, Wirtz; Morrison, Isak, Ngumoha.Substitutes: Woodman, Davies, Chiesa, Jones, Elliott, Tsimikas, Gravenberch, Abe, Ramsay, Scanlon, McConnell, Koumas, Ndiaye, Wright, Sonni-Lambie.

Leeds: Cairns; Justin, Muharemovic, Rodon; Bogle, Ampadu, Stach, Tanaka, Gudmundsson; James, Nmecha.Substitutes: Mahady, Ombang, Lane, Lienou, Cresswell, Bornauw, Crew, Longstaff, Aaronson, Gnonto, Pickles, Wilson, Chadwick, Mills, Calvert-Lewin, Piroe.

There was a lot to take in, during those madcap 42 seconds, but it was a scene that showed the full extent of the issues Andoni Iraola must address.

First came a handshake with Curtis Jones that the midfielder, lost in red mist, barely acknowledged. It was not impressive, shrugging off a new manager like that, but as Iraola strode across the field at Yankee Stadium, after Liverpool’s 1-0 win over Wrexham on Wednesday, the action really began.

Jones squawked and jabbed at his arm. Dominik Szoboszlai bellowed back, arms stretched out so wide you could not help but notice. Next came Kostas Tsimikas throwing the captain’s armband on the floor, landing at Jones’s feet, as Giorgi Mamardashvili and Jeremie Frimpong looked on awkwardly.

The French defender, who has arrived from Rennes this summer, is not involved for Liverpool today and is yet to feature for his new club so far this pre-season as he is eased in after a shoulder injury days after his move to Liverpool was confirmed earlier this year.

Our team to take on Leeds United 🙌Watch the game LIVE on All Red Video:

Soldier Field in Chicago hosts an all-Premier League tie encounter as Liverpool take on Leeds as both sides bring their US tours to a close. Both Premier League encounters between these sides last season ended in draws; a 3-3 draw at Elland Road was followed up by a 0-0 stalemate at Anfield. The draw at Elland Road was immediately followed by Mohamed Salah speaking to the media, claiming he had been thrown under the bus.

It is a new era at Liverpool as former Bournemouth boss Andoni Iraola has replaced Arne Slot at Anfield. They kicked off the Iraola era in Nashville, Tennessee, with a 4-2 win over Sunderland, following that up with another victory in New York on Wednesday night, beating Wrexham 1-0, and will be aiming to make it three wins from three on their US tour.

“I think it [the US tour] has been really, really useful,” Iraola said in an interview on the official Liverpool website. Obviously, you spend a lot of time with the players, with the staff, you get all the information you can. And I think there is also an evolution, it has to be. We start to understand each other better, what we need to do. Every game, I hope we can get closer and closer and put ourselves in a position where the few players that still are not here start to train also, they are helped by the others.”

Virgil van Dijk and Cody Gakpo resumed training back on Merseyside whilst Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Victor Munoz are yet to return to training following their World Cup exploits. The trio of Florian Wirtz, Alexander Isak and Ryan Gravenberch are all set to feature for the first time this pre-season.

Leeds’ pre-season campaign began with a 3-2 loss to Championship Wrexham in Tampa, Florida before beating Sunderland 1-0 in New Jersey courtesy of a long-range strike from Lukas Nmecha. Former Liverpool man Harry Wilson joined Leeds on a free from Fulham this summer.

“Really tough but that is expected,” Wilson said. That is what pre-season is for, building up a base for when the season starts, making sure you are in the best physical position you can be to attack the season. It has been good. I played against them [Leeds] twice last year when I was at Fulham. Both games were really, really tough games.

“I think when the fans have got a good team to support, I think that [the atmosphere at Elland Road] goes up a notch. I think the size of the club was a massive part of me coming. Then speaking to the guys, the chairman, the sporting director, and seeing kind of the plans and the aims for the club, it is something I wanted to be a part of.”

#2269. “The desire is there on all sides” – Thioune hopeful of permanent Füllkrug deal as West Ham hold the key

Werder Bremen coach Daniel Thioune has made it clear that the Bundesliga side want to keep Niclas Füllkrug beyond the end of his loan spell from West Ham, which expires in the summer.

However, Thioune also pointed to the financial considerations and the role of Füllkrug's parent club.

“I think the desire is there on all sides," Thioune told Transfermarkt.

"He doesn't feel under pressure to prove himself; rather, he is eager to show what he can do. Of course, it then becomes a question of what West Ham want and what they are willing and able to do. And we have to be equally honest about our own situation: What are we capable of, and what is Niclas willing to do?

"But we, as a club, I as a coach, and Niclas himself are all very interested in continuing to work together beyond the summer.”

Werder Bremen managing director Klaus Filbry recently expressed the club's hopes of retaining the striker as well.

“Of course, West Ham are an important third party in this situation. The league Werder are playing in at the end of the season will also play a role. Nevertheless, I remain cautiously optimistic that we can ultimately make the deal happen,” Filbry told Bild.

With nine goals in nine Bundesliga appearances, Füllkrug currently leads the German top-flight scoring charts.

#2268. Pedro sulla Lazio di Gattuso: «La città e i tifosi della Lazio meritano»

Lo spagnolo si augura che la squadra conservi il rendimento attuale; sul ritiro racconta le difficoltà di recupero.

Pedro è felice per la Lazio prima in classifica e riconosce l’impatto di Gennaro Gattuso sulla squadra. Intervistato da Cadena SER nel programma El Larguero, l’ex biancoceleste ha parlato del gioco dei suoi vecchi compagni e della decisione di chiudere la carriera al termine della scorsa stagione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Pedro ha raccontato come è maturata la decisione: «Inizialmente pensavo di aspettare ancora un po’ per capire se sarebbe arrivata qualche possibilità di continuare, ma con il tempo ho capito quanto mi facesse stare bene avere più spazio per la famiglia e gli amici». Sul piano fisico, ha aggiunto: «Ho scelto in base alle sensazioni fisiche: nell’ultima stagione recuperare dopo le partite e ritrovare il ritmo era diventato sempre più complicato».

Pedro ne ha parlato con le persone a lui più vicine e ha maturato la scelta senza viverla come una conseguenza di un malessere: «A un certo punto della carriera bisogna ascoltare questi segnali. Ne ho parlato con le persone più vicine e ho deciso con serenità, perché non stavo male: semplicemente ho ritenuto fosse arrivato il momento giusto».

Guardando alla posizione occupata oggi dalla Lazio, Pedro ha scherzato sulla propria assenza: «Vedere la Lazio prima senza di me mi fa pensare che forse avrei dovuto partire prima… oppure restare un’altra stagione!». Poi ha chiarito il senso delle sue parole: «Scherzi a parte, sono davvero felice per loro. Si vede quanto abbia inciso Gattuso e sento parlare molto bene del suo lavoro».

#2266. Mykhailo Mudryk returns as Chelsea slip to Juventus defeat

Mykhailo Mudryk made his first Chelsea appearance since November 2024 as Xabi Alonso’s team succumbed to their second pre-season defeat.

Mudryk replaced Nicolas Jackson in the 82nd minute against Juventus, marking his return to competitive football after a long doping ban that was resolved this week thanks to changes in Wada regulations.

There were a couple of crosses delivered from the left flank by the Ukrainian winger, who could yet leave Chelsea on loan or on a permanent basis before the close of the transfer window.

Juventus were the victors though, thanks to a sumptuous 68th-minute goal by Kosovo winger Edon Zhegrova.

Alonso had 21 players on his bench, and made 12 second-half substitutions.

Levi Colwill and Cole Palmer featured in the defeat by 10-man Spurs on Saturday, but sat this game out as they continue to build fitness. Danny Welbeck did start though, reunited with former Brighton team-mate Joao Pedro up top.

Chelsea scored just one goal against Spurs and Juventus, but the thrust provided by right-back Marco Palestra in tandem with first Geovany Quenda and then Estevao was a bright spot for Alonso.

Chelsea continue their pre-season against AC Milan on Saturday, before they host Real Sociedad at Stamford Bridge on August 15.

They begin their Premier League campaign at Fulham in the Monday night slot on the opening weekend.

Even Chelsea’s in-house streaming had given up the ghost by the end. Consecutive pre-season defeats for Chelsea, but worth remembering that Colwill and Palmer sat out this fitness exercise and Enzo Fernandez is still to return. Palestra’s performances a real positive but the team is still finding its way.

Juventus win a corner late on, but Yildiz’s delivery is too close to Penders. Just two minutes for Chelsea to find an equaliser.

Mudryk does well to dig out a cross from the left but the goalkeeper Perin gathers. There will be four minutes of added time to play.

Chelsea not really threatening an equaliser as the game meanders towards a conclusion. Should they score a goal, we will have a penalty shoot-out.

Estevao looked for Mudryk with a reverse pass between full-back and centre-back but there was too much weight on the ball.

Estevao’s free-kick is saved but the bigger news for Chelsea fans is that Mykhailo Mudryk has been introduced from the bench, replacing Nicolas Jackson for the closing stages.

Lavia and Liam Delap involved in some handbags with the Juventus players, Bremer the centre-back in the thick of things too and has been shown a yellow card. Chelsea have a free-kick, Estevao over it from 35 yards out.

Just the one goal scored for Chelsea against top level opponents in pre-season, but I doubt Alonso will be panicking just yet. Chelsea play Milan this weekend before hosting Real Sociedad on August 15th in their final pre season friendly.

Juventus goalkeeper Perin sells Nicolas Jackson a dummy so he can pick a pass into midfield. The Italian side controlling the game quite well since the goal, against a weaker Chelsea team.

Chelsea’s younger players will have to dig them out of trouble in the last 20 minutes. There has not been much in the game, Chelsea have shaded it in general play without quite creating enough.

The Kosovan winger with a first-time, left-footed hit from almost 25 yards, curled into the top corner. Nothing Penders could do about it.

More changes from Chelsea: Anselmino, Acheampong, Satpaev, Assugo and Delap the players on, replacing Hato, Palestra, Gittens, Caicedo and Pedro. Alonso finishing the team with his younger players on the pitch.

Jonathan David slides a pass across the Chelsea six-yard box when there was a chance to shoot, but the flag was up for offside in any case.

Penders does well to palm away an inswinging cross from Zhegrova, before Estevao picks out the run of Palestra on the break with a brilliant forward pass. Chelsea corner, cleared. Now Caicedo has been booked for a cynical challenge to stop a break, much like Douglas Luiz.

Nicolas Jackson hacked down by Douglas Luiz after he turned on halfway with three or four Chelsea runners in support. Painful one for Jackson, and a yellow card for the former Aston Villa midfielder. Chelsea players not happy with that challenge in a pre-season game.

Chelsea certainly have the upper hand in the game, quick feet from Joao Pedro to win a free-kick in midfield. If either team is going to score the game’s first goal, you fancy it will be them.

This time Chelsea find Palestra with a ball over the top, but his shot at goal is at a comfortable height for the goalkeeper.

Palestra popping up in a centre-forward position again, but his shot towards goal is not struck cleanly. The right-back at the heart of Chelsea’s attacking again.

Two very different XIs out there for the second half.

Penders replaces Sanchez in goal, Sarr on for Tosin, Estevao on for Quenda and Jackson on for Welbeck.

For Juventus: Bremer, Perin, Zhegrova, Owusu and David are on.

Not much to write/phone/WhatsApp home about, so far. The combination between Quenda and Palestra down Chelsea’s right has been the best feature of their football, am sure we will see Estevao on that flank in the second half among other changes. The bumpy pitch and a hydration break has not helped the spectacle.

There will be four minutes of stoppage time, simply a result of the hydration break.

Far too much space opens up between Chelsea’s defence and midfield, with Meritti turning and carrying the ball forward. Boga tests Sanchez with a strike from the edge of the box. That was probably Juventus’s most threatening attack.

Palestra defends well as the last man up against Milik, Chelsea almost undone by Locatelli’s outside of the foot pass.

Robert Sanchez caught under a cross swung to the back post, very unconvincing goalkeeping, but Juventus could not get their shot away in the box. Nicoll-Jazuli then did well to bring the ball away for Chelsea at the edge of the box.

Chelsea have another corner, and yet again it comes from a right-sided attack. Chelsea are in ascendancy now after a slow start, but it is a very low intensity contest.

Caicedo with a couple of threatening crosses from a centre-right position, but no Chelsea player can connect with them cleanly. Gittens’s dribbling down the left causing problems for Cambiaso, and he was the one attacking Caicedo’s cross at the back post.

Play has now resumed after the drinks break. No changes from either team, those will come at half time. Chelsea have 21 players sitting on their bench, albeit a number of academy players are on tour.

Time for a hydration break, even though the game is being played under a closed roof.

Chelsea’s right side is their most dangerous, by a distance. Quenda does well to slip Palestra in on the overlap, and his low cross into the six-yard box is cleared for a corner. Juventus clear. Boga with a burst through the Chelsea midfield but the Juventus man then gets his pass wrong.

Kelly with a left-to-right switch to Cambiaso, and his cross deflects off the toe of Miretti in the middle and trickles just wide of the far post. Sanchez was scrambling but I think the goalkeeper had it covered.

Chelsea enjoying their most sustained spell of possession in Juventus’s half so far, without quite carving out a clear cut chance. Juventus defending their penalty area with a back five, but they do not have Bonucci, Chiellini and Barzagli back there anymore.

Quenda with a threatening inswinging cross from the right flank, but Welbeck could not quite rise high enough to direct his header towards the far corner. Quenda was keeping the width for Chelsea with Palestra inside the winger in the box. Quenda then slices a shot over from long range.

Welbeck and Caicedo involved in some good combination play, with Nicoll-Jazuli’s outside of the foot pass finding Gittens. Chelsea’s left-winger runs into traffic, but he has been one of the bright spots of the pre-season campaign thus far.

Having watched a couple of Chelsea’s friendlies, there is a lot to like about Palestra at right-back. Tall, long stride, lots of composure on the ball. Will be interesting to see if they can find a way for him and Reece James to start games. Chelsea as a team yet to find much rhythm in the game so far.

Tosin could well find himself down the pecking order this season among Chelsea’s raft of centre-backs, but he makes an important block in the area before Locatelli drags a shot wide from the edge of the box.

Former Bournemouth defender Lloyd Kelly is in the Juventus team. The Italian team are looking to press high in the early minutes whenever Chelsea try to play out from the back. Quenda with an early dart at the Juventus defence but he gets the pass all wrong with Palestra overlapping.

Palestra with a loose first touch but he recovers and defends well. Like in Sydney, this looks another very bumpy pitch, you can see the join marks between the pieces of turf that have been freshly laid. Coming out of these games without any injuries will be a priority for Alonso.

Juventus get the game started in their pale pink away kit.

Juventus XI: Di Gregorio, Kalulu, Gatti, Kelly, Cambiaso, Douglas Luiz, Locatelli, Miretti, Boga, Milik, Celik

Subs: Perrin, Pinsoglio, Nava, Bremmer, Rugani, Koopmeiners, Arthur Melo, Cabal, Owusu, Gil Puche, Oboavwoduo, Licina, Durmisi, Yildiz, Zhegrova, David

Welbeck starts against Juventus, but no Jordan Henderson with the group just yet. As Sam Dean writes here: “Last season, especially, provided evidence that the balance of their squad was not right, and they are now trying to change the internal dynamic by adding more leadership and experience to the team.”

How long will he stay there? Will he play his way back into Alonso’s team, be shipped out on loan or sold for a fee? Sam Dean assesses the options for player and club in this piece. Out of sight, out of mind could well be the most likely outcome for a player who has missed almost two years of football, and looked extremely raw before his ban.

Looks like a back four once again for Alonso, and Danny Welbeck makes his first Chelsea appearance. Pedro will play off Welbeck as a second striker. Geovany Quenda was signed last year from Sporting CP, but joined up with Chelsea this summer. Another wide forward in their collection.

Chelsea XI: Sanchez; Palestra, Fofana, Tosin, Hato; Caicedo, Nicoll-Jazuli; Quenda, Joao Pedro, Gittens; Welbeck

Chelsea subs: Penders, Sharman-Lowe, Curd, Slonina, Acheampong, Subuloye, Sarr, Diakite, Anselmino, Lavia, Essugo, Watson, Walsh, Kellyman, Mudryk, Estevao Willian, Kavuma-McQueen, Neto, Satpayev, Jackson, Delap

The wheels of commerce continue to turn for Chelsea in the transfer market but this afternoon Xabi Alonso’s team continue their preparations for the new season against Juventus in Hong Kong.

They have the chance to recover from the ignominy of losing to 10-man Tottenham Hotspur in Sydney on Saturday, but with 19 days until Chelsea’s Premier League opener against Fulham these matches are still a fitness building exercise. The positive from the Spurs game was Wesley Fofana, Levi Colwill, Cole Palmer completing 80 minutes – three players who endured injury problems last season.

Another new arrival is expected to follow Morgan Rogers, Marco Palesta, Maxence Lacroix, Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck to Stamford Bridge, with the club nearing a deal for Rayo Vallecano left-back Pep Chavarria.

It wouldn’t be Chelsea without talk of some eye-catching outgoings, with Spurs reportedly interested in Nicolas Jackson and Enzo Maresca eyeing a reunion with Pedro Neto at Manchester City.

Alonso’s team promise to be flexible in their tactical approach this season, but so far he has set up with a back four rather than the 3-4-2-1 system he used to such great effect at Bayer Leverkusen. That could change as availability increases closer to the start of the season, but Palestra’s bursts forward from right-back in tandem with Estevao have caught the eye.

Juventus finished sixth in Serie A last season under Luciano Spalletti, the former Roma and Napoli coach who usually guarantees expansive and attractive football. Turkey left-winger Kenan Yildiz was their top goalscorer last season, and it looks like they will make it through the summer without the left-winger being picked off by one of the Premier League’s elite. Yildiz scored 11 goals in all competitions, and Dusan Vlahovic was the only other player to reach double figures so scoring goals is a problem to address. Lois Openda and Randal Kolo Muani have been signed this summer to strengthen the forward line.

#2264. Lucas Hernandez de retour en équipe de France ? Zidane y pense...

Ce vendredi 6 novembre à 18h00, Zinédine Zidane annoncera sa deuxième liste à la tête de l'équipe de France depuis le siège de la FFF. Confronté à une avalanche de blessures, le sélectionneur tricolore s'apprête à repenser son secteur défensif... avec le retour de Lucas Hernandez ?

Pour aborder ce rassemblement capital en Ligue des nations, le staff technique des Bleus doit composer avec une cascade de forfaits majeurs dans ses lignes arrières. En effet, William Saliba n'est pas disponible pour cette échéance internationale, le défenseur central étant tout juste revenu d'une blessure au dos. Un coup dur auquel s'ajoute l'absence prolongée de Maxence Lacroix. Forfait en raison d'une déchirure aux ischio-jambiers, le joueur pourrait même être absent jusqu'à la fin de l'année. Enfin, Jules Koundé est également annoncé indisponible pour ces rendez-vous de novembre, n'étant pas encore remis de son entorse de la cheville gauche. Un casse-tête défensif.

Face à ces défections d'envergure, Zinédine Zidane explorerait plusieurs solutions d'expérience et de polyvalence pour rebâtir son arrière-garde. D'après L'Équipe, Lucas Hernandez et Castello Lukeba feraient ainsi partie des joueurs pressentis pour créer la surprise dans le secteur défensif de cette deuxième liste. Le joueur du Paris Saint-Germain sort d'une période positive avec la formation parisienne et offre une solution très appréciable dans l'axe ou à gauche. De son côté, Castello Lukeba possède un registre similaire. Le pensionnaire du RB Leipzig présente également l'avantage tactique de pouvoir évoluer dans l'axe central ainsi qu'au poste de latéral gauche. Une opportunité idéale pour les Bleus.

Au-delà de ces deux recours polyvalents, un autre profil inattendu pourrait créer l'événement dans le couloir gauche de la défense tricolore. Selon Foot Mercato, le latéral gauche Dayann Méthalie, qui évolue actuellement à Sunderland, a également reçu une pré-convocation de la part du staff des Bleus. Reste à savoir si le sélectionneur validera définitivement cette option ce vendredi à 18h00. Cette équipe de France renouvelée sera rapidement mise à l'épreuve lors des deux derniers matches de phase de poules de Ligue des nations. Les hommes de Zidane défieront l'Italie le 12 novembre à Milan à 20h45, avant de retrouver la Turquie le 15 novembre à Bordeaux à 20h45.

#2263. Lazio-Reggina, Gentile sulla multiproprietà: «Vedrete, le cose andranno in porto»

Il legale di Lotito indica la strada per superare il divieto di multiproprietà e si dice ottimista sul futuro della Reggina.

Lazio e Reggina, la questione della multiproprietà torna al centro dell'attenzione. A parlarne è l'avvocato Gian Michele Gentile, legale di fiducia del presidente biancoceleste Claudio Lotito, che mostra grande ottimismo sulla possibilità di superare l'attuale ostacolo.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La strada indicata passa attraverso una riforma delle NOIF, che permetterebbe di modificare l'attuale situazione relativa alla multiproprietà. Gentile guarda già alla scadenza fissata al termine della stagione e utilizza parole particolarmente significative: «Vedrete che le cose programmate andranno in porto».

Secondo quanto riportato da Radio Touring 104, Gentile ha affrontato la questione nel corso di un'intervista nella quale ha parlato anche dell'operazione Reggina, delle motivazioni di Lotito e delle prospettive della società calabrese.

Il legale del presidente della Lazio ha spiegato quale sarebbe la strada per affrontare il problema della multiproprietà, collegandola anche alla possibilità di valorizzare maggiormente i calciatori italiani.

«Multiproprietà? L'ostacolo si supera con una riforma delle Noif. Secondo l'idea di Claudio Lotito, è un modo per valorizzare calciatori italiani in ottica Nazionale. Prendendo spunto dalla Salernitana. Con calciatori arrivati dalla Serie C fino alla Serie A. Poi Lotito ha dovuto svendere la Salernitana. L'obiettivo della riforma è di far partecipare e crescere numerosi calciatori, che non avrebbero tale possibilità se continuassero a giocare in traballanti realtà di Lega Pro. Senza sbocchi professionali. Non è una riforma per Lotito».

Gentile ha quindi affrontato direttamente l'investimento effettuato sulla Reggina, ribadendo le intenzioni del presidente biancoceleste.

«Lotito non fa le cose tanto per farle. Se ha preso la Reggina, è per farle ottenere il miglior risultato. Il problema sarà quello di eliminare il divieto di multiproprietà. Una riforma consentirebbe l'accesso alla Serie C».

Dietro l'operazione ci sarebbe stata anche una componente sentimentale, legata alle origini della famiglia Lotito.

«La trattativa per la Reggina è stata sentimentale. La famiglia di Lotito ha origini calabresi. Il sindaco di Reggio Calabria ha premuto moltissimo per raggiungere un accordo».

Il legale ha poi ricostruito alcuni aspetti della situazione economica trovata al momento dell'operazione.

«Abbiamo verificato la situazione, sia pure sommariamente. La società che fa capo a Lotito si è impegnata a sanare le passività. Tutto nel giro di 10 o 15 giorni, con grande soddisfazione di tutti».

Gentile ha specificato anche la natura delle pendenze: «Stipendi non pagati e anticipazioni degli ex soci. Roba ordinaria, compatibile con la gestione di una società di calcio in difficoltà sportiva».

Infine, un'altra precisazione: «La Rhegium è stata creata da Lotito».

#2262. « Je ne me sens coupable de rien » : Jorge Jesus réagit à la décision de Cristiano Ronaldo

Présent ce vendredi 6 novembre 2026 en conférence de presse à la Cidade do Futebol à Oeiras pour dévoiler sa liste de 28 joueurs, Jorge Jesus a tenu à clarifier la situation autour de Cristiano Ronaldo. Le sélectionneur portugais a en effet révélé n'avoir appris la retraite internationale de son attaquant que le jeudi 5 novembre 2026, au moment de la publication de sa vidéo et de son communiqué officiel.

Ce vendredi, la Cidade do Futebol à Oeiras a été le théâtre d'une annonce particulièrement attendue. Avant que Jorge Jesus ne présente sa convocation pour les rencontres de Ligue des nations face au Danemark et au pays de Galles, la vidéo d'adieu de Cristiano Ronaldo a été diffusée dans l'auditorium, précédée d'un hommage de Pedro Proença, le président de la Fédération portugaise de football. Mais alors que le dirigeant fédéral était dans la confidence selon la presse portugaise, le sélectionneur national l'a découvert lui en même temps que tout le monde.

Le technicien lusitanien, sous contrat avec la Fédération portugaise de football jusqu'en 2030, avait initialement prévu d'intégrer l'attaquant de 41 ans dans son groupe de 28 joueurs. Jorge Jesus n'avait pas cherché à lui téléphoner en amont, persuadé que le joueur poursuivrait l'aventure lors de cette phase de poules. Une surprise totale. Face aux journalistes, l'entraîneur a raconté sans détour les coulisses de ce dénouement :

Cette annonce intervient un mois après de vives tensions au sein du vestiaire portugais. Lors du précédent rassemblement, Cristiano Ronaldo avait reproché à Jorge Jesus de ne pas l'avoir fait entrer face à la Norvège, avant de s'agacer de l'absence d'excuses en conférence de presse et de claquer la porte. Interrogé sur d'éventuels regrets concernant la gestion de cet épisode, le sélectionneur a balayé tout remords : « Rien. Zéro. Parce que j'ai pris une décision d'entraîneur. »

D'ailleurs, le sélectionneur a tenu à évacuer toute idée de conflit personnel avec celui qui met un terme à sa carrière internationale après 23 ans sous le maillot portugais, cumulant 234 sélections et 146 buts. « Si j'ai dit que j'envisageais de le convoquer, c'est parce que je pensais qu'il allait poursuivre le projet de Ligue des nations. Il n'y a aucune animosité », a rappelé le patron de la Seleção, assurant ne porter aucune culpabilité dans cette issue.

C'est un changement majeur pour la sélection portugaise. Afin d'assurer la continuité sportive et symbolique, Jorge Jesus a confirmé que le brassard de capitaine revenait à Bernardo Silva, joueur le plus capé du groupe présent, conformément à la tradition de la Seleção. Au-delà de ce passage de témoin, le sélectionneur a profité de ce rassemblement pour rajeunir son effectif. Ainsi, deux nouveaux éléments font leur apparition pour la première fois : le latéral droit Alberto Costa (FC Porto) et l'attaquant Gustavo Varela (Monza).

L'équipe nationale doit désormais se focaliser sur ses prochains rendez-vous sur le terrain. Le Portugal recevra le Danemark le samedi 14 novembre 2026 à 20h45 à l'Estádio Municipal de Braga pour la 5e journée de la Ligue des nations, avant d'affronter le pays de Galles le mardi 17 novembre 2026 à 20h45 au Cardiff City Stadium.

#2261. Bellinazzo: "Rosso Juve preoccupante, modello non sostenibile. A rigor di logica..."

Bellinazzo: "Rosso Juve preoccupante, modello non sostenibile. A rigor di logica..."

Installa la nostra App gratuita e accedi più velocemente alle notizie

Mentre navighi nell'app, scorri il dito da sinistra a destra dello schermo per tornare alle pagine precedenti

Scegli Fcinter1908.it come tuo sito preferito su Google: clicca qui

Marco Bellinazzo, giornalista de il Sole 24 Ore, ha commentato i dati emersi dal bilancio della Juventus, che ha chiuso il 2025-2026 con una perdita di 66 mln di euro:

"L’idea da cui si è partiti, evidentemente, era quella di provare a ridurre i costi, puntando su una partecipazione in questi anni il più possibile assidua alla Champions League. Considerando il fatto che i ricavi dell'Europa League equivalgono, in proporzione, a un quinto di quelli della Champions, è evidente che questo rosso è frutto di due fattori. Da un lato, appunto, la necessità di abbassare i costi senza depauperare il patrimonio tecnico della squadra, per agganciare la Champions. E di conseguenza sono stati evidentemente commessi degli errori, visto che l'anno scorso questo risultato non è stato ottenuto. Dall'altro lato, la necessità di tenere il più possibile a galla il club, considerando gli impegni assunti con la UEFA. Quindi è un rosso, per rispondere in maniera secca, preoccupante, nell'ottica in cui, pur essendoci delle note positive nel bilancio dello scorso anno, il mancato accesso alla Champions di questa stagione complica un po' le cose. Non a caso, questo bilancio è stato il preludio a un aumento di capitale molto consistente, da 250 milioni di euro".

È un'operazione necessaria per garantire la sostenibilità del club o serve piuttosto a finanziare nuovi investimenti?

"Diciamo che risponde a entrambe le logiche. È stato dichiarato come obiettivo duplice dalla stessa proprietà, tant'è che Exor si è impegnata a sottoscriverlo integralmente, anche in caso di mancata sottoscrizione da parte degli altri soci. Ed è oggettivamente quello che risulta guardando il bilancio, i numeri e le proiezioni. Il fabbisogno del club per allinearsi ai parametri della UEFA assorbirà intorno ai 150 milioni, mentre ci sarà la possibilità di intervenire con il resto sul mercato. Questo perché, alla luce di quello che abbiamo detto, per la Juve sarà fondamentale, ma ormai è un aggettivo che si usa un po' per tutti i top club, agganciare i primi quattro posti per la prossima Champions League. Quindi ci sono da aspettarsi, a rigor di logica, degli interventi importanti a gennaio, proprio in funzione di questo inseguimento dei primi quattro posti".

Si parla di sostenibilità, ma negli ultimi anni Exor ha versato all’incirca un miliardo nelle casse della Juventus. È sostenibile un modello di questo tipo?

"È evidente che, nel momento in cui parliamo di una società che brucia cassa e che va in perdita sistematicamente, il modello non è sostenibile. Ma lo sa benissimo anche il nuovo management della Juventus. Tant'è che l'intesa di fatto raggiunta con la UEFA, con il settlement agreement, prevede un rientro il più possibile rapido all'interno dei parametri economico-finanziari. La Juve, in effetti, sforava il parametro della cosiddetta football earnings rule, cioè il limite di perdite di 60 milioni nel triennio, ma rispettava e rispetta il parametro del costo del lavoro allargato, la squad cost rule. Quindi l'ammontare degli ingaggi, degli ammortamenti dei cartellini e dei costi degli intermediari è comunque all'interno del parametro del 70% del fatturato complessivo, che include i ricavi caratteristici e la media triennale delle plusvalenze. La Juve, quindi, sfora da una parte, ma per fortuna rispetta l'altro parametro. E questo risponde proprio a una consapevolezza e alle misure che sono state adottate per tenere almeno la squad cost rule sotto il 70%. Parametro che, ricordo, oggi è applicato anche in Italia, nel fair play finanziario made in Italy, ma che per il momento vale soltanto ai fini del calciomercato e non ai fini dell'iscrizione al campionato".

#2260. « C'était pareil avec Vettel et Sainz » : Toujours en colère, Hamilton règle ses comptes avec Leclerc chez Ferrari

À São Paulo avant le Grand Prix du Brésil, Lewis Hamilton a haussé le ton contre Charles Leclerc. Toujours marqué par le scénario du Grand Prix du Mexique, le pilote britannique a pointé du doigt l'agressivité de son équipier chez Ferrari, coupable selon lui d'en faire bien trop contre sa propre monoplace.

Dimanche 1er novembre 2026, la Scuderia Ferrari disposait d'une occasion en or sur l'Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez. Parti en pole position aux côtés de Charles Leclerc, qualifié au troisième rang, Lewis Hamilton espérait concrétiser la domination des monoplaces italiennes. Mais dès les premiers virages de Mexico, les deux partenaires se sont livrés une passe d'armes acharnée roue contre roue. En virant trop large, les deux monoplaces ont quitté brièvement la piste, manquant de peu l'accrochage. Sanctionné d'une pénalité de cinq secondes pour avoir quitté la piste et conservé un avantage durable lors de son dépassement, Charles Leclerc a vu Max Verstappen (Red Bull) s'intercaler et rafler la victoire. Lewis Hamilton a terminé deuxième et Charles Leclerc quatrième. Un immense gâchis.

Cette passe d'armes a provoqué la fureur immédiate de Frédéric Vasseur. Le directeur de la Scuderia Ferrari a fustigé la manœuvre au micro de Canal+ : « Ce n'est pas le résultat qu'on espère, surtout quand on est premier et deuxième après le premier virage. À Mexico, il n'y a pas eu un dépassement depuis 72 ans donc on n'espère pas finir deuxième et quatrième... J'ai du mal à l'avaler car je pense que c'est un manque de respect pour la marque, pour tous les gens qui travaillent, les efforts qu'on fait. » Le dirigeant n'a pas caché sa colère pour les 2 000 salariés de l'écurie après la perte de cette victoire promise. Charles Leclerc a d'ailleurs reconnu son erreur au micro de Canal+ : « La pénalité est clairement méritée. On ne fait tous les deux pas le virage, on freine tous les deux trop tard. Mon objectif était de redonner la position à Lewis mais Max (Verstappen) s'est intercalé entre nous donc ça devenait difficile. On va en discuter. »

Présent devant les journalistes à São Paulo, Lewis Hamilton n'a pas éludé le sujet. Le pilote britannique a accusé publiquement Charles Leclerc d'afficher une agressivité ciblée contre lui en piste, bien supérieure à celle réservée à leurs adversaires de Red Bull, McLaren ou Mercedes. Interrogé sur le comportement du Monégasque, Lewis Hamilton a dressé une comparaison sans détour avec les saisons passées de la Scuderia : « Je vois la même chose que vous. À Singapour, il était parfaitement [à la hauteur de Verstappen], roue contre roue, totalement à l'intérieur pour la prise de tête au virage 1 ; et je pense que c'était vraiment une situation différente. Si l'on regarde ses coéquipiers, c'était pareil avec Sebastian (Vettel) et avec Carlos (Sainz) », a lâché Lewis Hamilton.

Le Britannique a affirmé être toujours frustré et agacé par la manœuvre de son voisin de garage, alors que l'écurie italienne avait les armes pour s'imposer en Amérique centrale. Il a ainsi prévenu qu'une explication franche attendait son équipier : « J'étais évidemment frustré et je le suis toujours. On doit avoir une discussion et on l'aura en temps voulu à notre retour en Europe. Nous avions l'occasion de gagner pour l'équipe qui a fait un boulot incroyable en nous tirant vers le haut cette année. »

Toutefois, les deux hommes n'ont pas encore pu échanger de vive voix au Brésil. Charles Leclerc était en effet absent de la journée médias à São Paulo le jeudi 5 novembre 2026 en raison de la naissance de sa fille. L'ambiance s'annonce tendue dans le garage transalpin alors que Ferrari aborde la dernière ligne droite de la saison. Au classement des constructeurs, l'écurie italienne occupe la deuxième place avec 126 points de retard sur Mercedes, dont le pilote Kimi Antonelli a été couronné champion du monde des pilotes au Mexique. Au classement des pilotes, Lewis Hamilton figure au troisième rang, deux points derrière Max Verstappen, tandis que Charles Leclerc est cinquième.

Au-delà des rancœurs nées à Mexico, la Scuderia doit impérativement se remobiliser pour sécuriser ses positions au championnat. La prochaine course est le Grand Prix de São Paulo sur le circuit d'Interlagos, dont le départ est prévu le dimanche 8 novembre 2026 à 18h00 heure française (14h00 heure locale).

#2259. ​Arteta’s ‘dynasty’ dream collides with Arsenal’s harsh reality

Mikel Arteta says he wants to create a “dynasty” at Arsenal as he threw down the gauntlet to his players to retain their Premier League title and reach a “different level”.

Arsenal are on the verge of completing a £75m deal for Brazil midfielder Bruno Guimãraes from Newcastle and have not given up hope of landing Real Madrid winger Vinícius Júnior, who has been offered an improved contract by the Spanish giants.

The Premier League champions slumped to a 3-1 defeat to Real Betis in Dublin on Wednesday night, when they paid the price for individual errors and a lethargic, sloppy defensive display.

But that did little to quell Arteta’s ambitions for the new season. “I’m even more excited [about this season], and we’re going to go and attack every possible title because that’s the ambition that we have,” he said.

“We know that we have the ability. We will go from a strength to a strength as well, whether it’s with the players that we have to take them to a different level, and with the market that is still open to recruit as well, so we are very optimistic about it.

“All the work that we’ve done – that I’ve done through the summer – is to understand what we need to do to win again and to create a dynasty in this football club. That’s the aim.”

Despite Arteta’s bullishness, he conceded Arsenal would have to be a lot better than they were against Betis. When asked about the mood in the dressing room, he said: “Very upset, given a hard time. They are fuming, but this is good. That’s what we need.”

Telegraph Sport analyses some of the talking points from a disappointing evening at the Aviva Stadium.

The importance of goalkeeper David Raya and centre-backs William Saliba and Gabriel Magalhães to Arsenal hardly needs overstating. Their title success was built on the foundations provided by that triumvirate at the back.

Raya has yet to report back from holiday after Spain’s World Cup triumph and Saliba is facing an extended spell on the sidelines with a back injury. Gabriel did appear for the second half but, watching this, Arteta is unlikely to have been dissuaded from the belief he needs another top defender to compensate for the loss of Saliba.

It may have been only Arsenal’s second game of pre-season, so a degree of legginess was understandable.

But the ease with which they were cut open and overloaded by the Spanish side, and the volume of individual errors, did not sit comfortably with Arteta with just over a fortnight until they kick off their title defence at home to newly promoted Coventry City.

Only once in 63 matches last season did Arsenal concede three goals in a single game but they were fortunate Betis did not score more. “In the first half there are two different things: to play well and to compete,” said Arteta, who saw his side trail 3-1 at the interval.

“We did the first one quite well in a lot of moments but the compete part – especially in and around our box – was not to the standards to win a football match against a good side. It’s better to give them [the goals away] in a friendly match than an official match. It’s always good when you lose a match in pre-season because it creates a bit more fire in the belly.”

Kepa Arrizabalaga will not want to watch Betis’s first goal back in a hurry. The Arsenal goalkeeper may have got a slight nudge as he came for the ball at a corner but he was all over the place and never looked even in the vaguest control of the situation. Rodrigo Riquelme scored at the far post after the ball sailed over the keeper. Arteta called it a “really sloppy goal”. With former Leeds goalkeeper Illan Meslier having arrived on a free transfer as back-up to Raya, Kepa faces an uncertain future at Arsenal. Moments like this will not help his cause.

He did not feature much last season but is probably best remembered for his torrid showing in the Carabao Cup final defeat by Manchester City in March. He looked as unconvincing here as he did then, as the former Chelsea goalkeeper also sliced a clearance in the build up to Betis’s third goal. Before then, Kai Havertz had turned over possession cheaply from which Nelson Deossa set up former West Ham midfielder Pablo Fornals to score.

Arsenal need more creativity and firepower in attack, hence the interest in Vinícius and Atlético Madrid’s Julián Alvarez. Viktor Gyokeres again looked rather limited here and the likes of Bukayo Saka and Eberechi Eze are also still to report back. Yet one of the few, brighter aspects of Arsenal’s performances was the sight of the regal looking Riccardo Calafiori marauding forward from a very nominal left-back role.

If Arsenal are going to play more adventurously this season and try to ratchet up things in the entertainment stakes then Calafiori could have a big role to play, as long as Arteta can keep him fit. He can be a potent weapon galloping forward and there were clear glimpses of that here. Harnessing that talent while not compromising too much defensive security may be one of the manager’s challenges.

Louie Copley had only been on the pitch for nine minutes – a half-time substitute for Ben White – when the 19-year-old midfielder went down largely unchallenged with what looked like a troubling knee injury. Arteta admitted afterwards that the way the teenager fell to the ground was a concern and he looked in visible pain and distress as he was treated by the medical staff before being helped off the pitch.

The fear will be of some kind of ligament damage and Arteta confirmed Copley would be scanned on Thursday. “Quite worried to be fair for the kid because the mechanism doesn’t look very positive and the symptoms that he already has,” the manager said. “So we are going to have to wait and see for tomorrow’s scan. Touch wood that is not a bad one.”

🌴 @RealBetis_en's Hector Bellerin reacts to a 3-1 preseason win over his former club Arsenal"I spent 10 years over there always trying to help and see Arsenal where it belongs, and it's nice to finally face them with them being in that position" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/er3YtAysQb

“It is another opportunity for fitness. Coming into games against teams of good quality, it is important we get good fitness. It is a chance to build momentum for the season ahead. We are taking steps in the right direction. Of course, we want more from the performance and the results, but we take learnings and move on.

Possession: Arsenal 56%-44% Real BetisShots: 9-10Shots on target: 2-7Corners: 2-2

There is the final whistle in Dublin and Betis secure a 3-1 win over Arsenal at Aviva Stadium. Goals from Riquelme, Deossa and Fornals has led Manuel Pellegrini’s side to the victory. All four goals in the game came before the break.

And that's full time in Dublin 👏Real Betis claim a 3-1 win against Premier League champions Arsenal 🌴 pic.twitter.com/0XWByNdtgh

Jesus gets onto the end of a ball in behind, getting to it just before the byline, and delivers a dangerous cross but Natan does well on the stretch to clear.

Antony was booed when he came on and is also being booed whenever he touches the ball.

Arsenal have registered just two shots on target in this game and both of those came in the first half. They have not really looked like scoring since the break, with probably Jesus coming closest.

Double change for Betis as Morante and Gomez replace Riquelme and Bernal.

Bellerin squares the ball from the byline and picks out Riquelme near the penalty spot but the latter is unable to take advantage.

The changes keep coming for Arsenal as Gabriel and Martinelli, who have only recently returned from their breaks after the World Cup, go off after half an hour on the pitch. Nwaneri was the final member of the Arsenal starting XI to still be on but his night is over.

Up until this point, Manuel Pellegrini had made just one change but he now makes a triple substitution, which sees three former Premier League players come on. Former Leeds duo Firpo and Llorente come on as does ex-Manchester United forward Antony. There are a few boos from the Arsenal fans as Antony comes on.

Martinelli is played in down the left channel and gets onto the end of the ball inside the Betis box. He checks back and finds his compatriot Jesus on the edge of the box. Jesus tries to pick out the bottom corner but his shot goes just wide.

Isco should put Betis 4-1 up but tries to be too cute and clever. Former Arsenal man Bellerin delivers a cross from the right side of the box and picks out a free Isco in the six-yard box. Isco attempts an audacious flick rather than putting his foot through it and his effort is saved by Meslier. That should have been a goal.

Arsenal have changed nearly their entire starting XI whereas Betis have made just the one substitution thus far. Betis have played more games so far in pre-season, which probably explains the difference in the number of changes.

Salmon is deceived by a dummy by Riquelme and then brings the Betis man down, earning him a yellow card.

On the hour mark, Mikel Arteta is going to make a triple change, which feels like it was a plan going into the game. That includes Meslier coming on in goal in place of Kepa.

Copley is helped off by the two Arsenal medics, shaking his head and not putting any weight on his left leg, and is replaced by Julienne.

You have to hope that the knee injury to Louie Copley is not serious but judging by the way he went down largely unchallenged, his reaction and the way he was being helped down the tunnel it didn’t look too good. A tough moment for the youngster who had only been on the pitch nine minutes.

Play is halted as Copley has been down for a little while clutching at his left knee. He got his studs stuck in the ground and went down in some pain. The medics come on to check that left knee. He only came on at half-time but his night is over not even 10 minutes into the second half.

Nwaneri catches Bernal and if this was a competitive fixture than I think Nwaneri would perhaps have been booked for that challenge.

Those raft of changes from Mikel Arteta at half-time have seen just four of their starting XI remain on the pitch; Kepa, Calafiori, Lewis-Skelly and Nwaneri.

Arsenal have a corner early on in this second half as Vieira’s shot from distance deflects behind. The delivery from the left has too much on it, going over the heads of all the Arsenal players in the box, and Betis are able to clear.

Mikel Arteta has made a whole host of changes, which includes the likes of Jesus, Martinelli, Gabriel and Vieira coming on. Betis have brought the former Real Madrid man Isco on at the break.

Possession: Arsenal 63%-37% Real BetisShots: 5-7Shots on target: 2-6Corners: 1-2

Arsenal’s title triumph was built on that stout defence and conceding so few but there have been so many self-inflicted wounds here. The first and third goals came from dismal individual errors from Kepa and Havertz and the second - while a wonder strike - came after Arsenal had failed to clear their lines properly.

The first half is brought to an end and Real Betis take a 3-1 lead into the break.

Manuel Pellegrini’s side have their third goal of the night and restore their two-goal advantage. Havertz gives the ball away poorly deep inside his own half and the ball is played into Fornals. The former West Ham man has it on the edge of the box and has P Garcia in space to his right but opts to shoot. It is a clinical finish from Fornals as he picks out the bottom left corner and celebrates by crossing his arms to form irons, paying tribute to his days at West Ham.

"It's so so easy!" 🎙️The former West Ham man Pablo Fornals puts Real Betis 3-1 up against Arsenal 🌴🔨 pic.twitter.com/iyBeyS1nHd

Betis come close to restoring their two-goal advantage. Calafiori gives the ball away deep inside his own half and the ball is quickly moved onto P Garcia on the right side of the box. He opens up his body and curls a shot first time towards the far corner, forcing Kepa into the save down to his right.

Riquelme shoots from just outside the box and forces Kepa into a save down to his right.

Betis have one goal from a corner and now Arsenal do. Betis keeper Valles complains that he is being fouled by Havertz after Tzolis swung in the corner from the left and the ball comes through to Hincapie, who has the simplest of headers from inside the six-yard box.

Normal service is resumed with a Gunners goal from the corner 👏Piero Hincapié gives the @Arsenal fans reason to celebrate! 🔴 pic.twitter.com/b7h979i0Gv

Important block from P Garcia. Dowman cuts in from the right across the face of the penalty area and finds Tzolis in space to his left. Tzolis takes one touch before taking on the shot from inside the Betis box but P Garcia slides in with a crucial block.

That is quite the finish! Deossa receives the ball in a central position around 25 yards out. He takes a couple of touches before lashing a shot with his left foot. His effort flies into the top corner and Betis have a 2-0 lead. Considering the quality of the finish, I am surprised that Deossa did not celebrate more bearing in mind you do not score screamers like that every day!

Nelson Deossa...what a hit! 😱😱Real Betis double their lead over Arsenal with a stunning strike and Mikel Arteta doesn't look happy 🌴 pic.twitter.com/4J5QnjOury

Since Gyokeres misses that very good chance just a minute into the game, Arsenal have not really carved out many genuine opportunities in front of goal, other than that Tzolis wasted chance. Every time they reach the final third, they are lacking that cutting edge.

Calafiori’s role is interesting. He’s very nominally a left back but is routinely stepping into midfield and raiding forward, often ending up in positions you’d associate with a No. 10. It’s the kind of role Nico O’Reilly played under Pep Guardiola at Manchester City.

Valles is so, so lucky. The Betis keeper inexplicably passes the ball straight at Tzolis inside the Betis penalty area but Tzolis is unable to capitalise. That is a huge slice of luck for Valles as that was a ridiculous moment.

Betis have already scored one goal from a corner and they now have another corner after Nwaneri’s clearance behind. The inswinger is sent into a good area but this time Arsenal deal with the danger.

Arsenal were the better side in the early stages but Betis have grown into this and have taken confidence from that goal.

The first goal of the night goes the way of the Spaniards. The corner from the left should be dealt with by Kepa but the Arsenal keeper makes an absolute mess of it. The ball goes straight through him and comes to Riquelme at the far post. He takes one touch before firing into the net. Kepa is appealing for a free-kick but there is never a foul in there.

Real Betis strike first at the Aviva! 🌴Riquelme takes advantage of poor Arsenal defending at the corner to open the scoring 👀 pic.twitter.com/1ubVDayElP

That is dire goalkeeping from Kepa. He’s desperately tried to claim he was fouled but he just made a complete hash of it.

Betis have their first shot of the night. P Garcia receives it out on the right and cuts inside onto his left. The space opens up for him to shoot and he obliges, forcing Kepa into a save before the ball is smashed behind for a corner...

Calafiori may be on the teamsheet tonight for Arsenal at left-back but when they are in possession the Italian is moving into midfield. Lewis-Skelly, who is playing in the number six role, is dropping in between the two centre-backs when Arsenal have the ball.

Betis win a free-kick out on the left, with the chance to send it into the Arsenal penalty area for the first time tonight. It is clipped into a good area but Kepa is out of his goal to catch it.

Arsenal should be ahead one minute into the game with their first attack of the game. Havertz picks up the ball on the corner of the box out on the left and passes it inside to Gyokeres. The Swedish striker takes one touch before shooting from the edge of the six-yard box but his shot is saved. In reality, Gyokeres should not have given Valles in the Betis goal any chance of saving that one.

Both sides emerge from the tunnel, Arsenal led out by Ben White and Betis by former Arsenal man Hector Bellerin, and make their way past the Premier League trophy. We are moments away from kick-off in Dublin.

Arsenal: Kepa; White, Mosquera, Hincapie, Calafiori; Lewis-Skelly, Havertz, Nwaneri; Dowman, Gyokeres, Tzolis.

Real Betis: Valles, Bellerin, Bartra, Natan, F.Garcia; Bernal, Gnangoro, Fornals; P.Garcia, Riquelme, Deossa.

Final preparations 🤝 pic.twitter.com/J4S5kVXwMl

Real Betis manager Manuel Pellegrini speaks ahead of his side's pre-season test against Arsenal 🌴"I think we have a good game against a big team here" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/v4tR6FOKtW

🥁 Introducing... The Arsenal! pic.twitter.com/S7NcnkfNBZ

A special night for Irish Gunners tonight, so who better to describe what @Arsenal means to so many in Ireland than Liam Brady, Emma Byrne and David O'Leary 🔴🇮🇪"It's a class club" 🗣️ pic.twitter.com/Fgi2ztxgLG

Matchday ready 🔋 pic.twitter.com/pfemNXIF2H

In the building 🫡 pic.twitter.com/hNITeYh7Gj

A debut for our brand-new third kit 🙌 pic.twitter.com/ELENSDEik2

“When I see the training and how hungry they are for every training drill, that means everybody is ready to compete at the highest level. When you are a player of Arsenal, you compete for every title that is possible. It is not only about the Premier League, it is about all the competitions we are playing for. I see a clear mindset and everything, that everybody is on the same page to win titles here. I saw it from the first training and I think when you train like that in the game, it makes it even better. I came here ready, with my fitness level and I was happy that I could show it here as well. I want to be myself and to show on the pitch all the passion and desire to win because I really like to win games and to give everything.

“If I give 100% for every game and every duel, I think who does not like this? I think that is the best thing for a football player, and then you will always have the support from the supporters. I am thinking about how to improve and settle as fast as possible in the club, because I have the opportunity to train directly with the team from the beginning of the season, to play pre-season games and then to go to official games. This is a chance to play directly from the beginning and then it is up to me to show the qualities and what I can bring to the team. I am pretty confident I will show it in the next games.”

INS:Illan Meslier ⇠ Leeds, FreeChristos Tzolis ⇠ Club Brugge, £34m

Piero Hincapie’s move from Bayer Leverkusen was made permanent this summer.

OUTS:Leandro Trossard ⇢ Besiktas, £18mJakub Kiwior ⇢ Porto, £15m
